- Proposed amalgamation of A1 Agri Global Limited, B.N. Agritech Limited and Salasar Balaji Overseas Private Limited is intended to centralise procurement and inventory management, improve facility utilisation and strengthen working-capital and cash-flow management
- Strategic investment in Epitome Industries India Limited through Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares creates a pathway into oleochemicals, speciality ingredients and other value-added oil-derived products
- Ability to convert common agricultural and oil-based feedstocks into multiple products, applications and market channels, broadening monetisation opportunities

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-activity and single-product concentration — BRSR Section A reports one business activity, Trading of Edible Oils, at 100% of turnover, and one product line, wholesale trading of edible oils (NIC 46305), at 100% of turnover. There is no second revenue stream to absorb a downturn in edible-oil trading.
- Commodity price volatility across the agri-oils chain — The MD&A cautionary statement names commodity prices and market dynamics among the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. As a trader of refined soyabean oil, crude palm oil and crude soyabean oil the Company is directly exposed to price movement between purchase and sale, and the Corporate Governance Report states that commodity price and foreign exchange hedging is not applicable as the Company is not associated with hedging activities.
- Import dependence and trade-policy exposure of the Indian edible oil market — The MD&A notes that against estimated domestic edible oil production of 9.6 million tonnes in the 2025-26 oil year, imports were projected at around 16.7 million tonnes. Government policies, regulatory developments and changing global trade dynamics, all named in the cautionary statement, therefore transmit directly into sourcing economics.
- Execution and approval risk on the proposed Scheme of Amalgamation — The amalgamation of A1 Agri Global Limited, B.N. Agritech Limited and Salasar Balaji Overseas Private Limited is central to the stated strategy but remains subject to sanction by the National Company Law Tribunal despite receipt of the BSE NOC in March 2026 and CCI approval in April 2026. The Board also had to approve amendments to the Scheme in December 2025.
- Feasibility, capital-allocation and execution risk on the diversification agenda — The Company repeatedly qualifies its move into oleochemicals, ingredients, consumer FMCG, biofuels and palm-oil plantation as subject to feasibility, approvals, capital allocation and execution decisions, and its Important note on Strategic Statements warns these initiatives should not be read as currently operational or committed. The downstream pathway depends on Epitome Industries India Limited, an investee rather than a controlled manufacturing asset.
- Key-person dependence and a very thin organisational base — There were 06 permanent employees as on March 31, 2026, and the BRSR states the Company had no employees other than the Board of Directors and Key Managerial Personnel during the reporting period, and no workers. Permanent-employee turnover was 50% in FY2025-26 and 100% in FY2023-24. Board and KMP churn during the year included a CEO change, a director resignation and a CFO change.
- Regulatory compliance and listing-obligation lapses — BSE levied two Standard Operating Procedure fines during the year: INR 76,700 for delay in submitting financial results under Regulation 33 for the quarter and year ended March 31, 2025, and INR 1,22,720 for alleged non-submission of the Annual Report within the prescribed timeline, for which a waiver application is under correspondence with BSE.
- Related-party concentration and governance oversight burden — The 35th AGM notice seeks member approval for material related-party transactions including with B.N. Agritech Limited, potentially exceeding the INR 1000 Crore or 10% of consolidated turnover threshold, for a tenure of three years. Several counterparties are entities on which the Company own Key Managerial Personnel have significant influence or control, concentrating oversight responsibility on the Audit Committee and Board.
- Asset-light structure with no owned manufacturing capacity — The Corporate Governance Report states the Company does not have any plant at any location, and BRSR reports zero plants nationally and internationally against two offices. BRSR Principle 2 confirms no R&D or capex expenditure was incurred because the Company is engaged in trading activities. Value capture therefore rests on trading margins and on assets held by investee or transferor entities rather than an owned asset base.

business.body: The Company is an operating agri-oils enterprise whose business activities and interests span agricultural commodities, oilseeds, edible oils and related products. It currently participates in the trading of refined soyabean oil, crude palm oil and crude soyabean oil, primarily serving wholesale and business customers, while its broader operating scope extends across oilseeds, solvent extraction, extracted oil cakes, refined oils and allied value chains. Its stated ambition is to progressively integrate a larger part of the agri-oils value chain, from origin and sourcing through processing, refining, ingredients, oleochemicals and bio-based derivatives to consumer products and distribution.

outlook.body:
- Integrate the operating core: execute the proposed amalgamation of A1 Agri Global Limited, B.N. Agritech Limited and Salasar Balaji Overseas Private Limited, and strengthen procurement, inventory, facility, customer and working-capital linkages
- Scale value-added manufacturing: build participation in food ingredients, oleochemicals, specialty derivatives and allied downstream products, including through the strategic CCPS investment in Epitome Industries India Limited
- Deepen consumer participation: expand consumer-facing products and branded opportunities where the Company can build differentiated market positions
- Strengthen feedstock security: develop diversified sourcing and evaluate selective upstream integration, including origin-linked sourcing and palm-oil plantation opportunities, where economically attractive
- Improve capital and working-capital efficiency: align growth with disciplined capital allocation, cash-flow visibility and prudent balance-sheet management
- Build an institutional-grade platform: create governance, reporting, operating systems and scale suitable for long-term banking, institutional capital and strategic partnerships
- Progress from commodity participation to value-added manufacturing, from B2B supply to deeper customer and consumer engagement, and from individual operating businesses to a connected platform ('From Agriculture to Consumer. From Commodity to Specialty.')
- Build a longer-term business architecture spanning Agri & Sourcing, Edible Oils & Processing, Oilseed Co-products, Food Ingredients, Oleochemicals & Derivatives, Consumer FMCG, Biofuels & Green Products, and Distribution & Supply Chain, developed progressively rather than simultaneously
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company disclosed no manufacturing capex or capacity addition of its own during FY2025-26. The BRSR Section A operations table records zero plants (national and international) and two offices, and the Corporate Governance Report states plainly that 'The Company does not have any plant at any location.' BRSR Principle 2 confirms the position: 'Not Applicable; The Company is engaged in trading activities and did not incur any expenditure on R&D and Capex.' Expansion is therefore being pursued through corporate structure rather than own-built assets. First, the proposed Scheme of Amalgamation of A1 Agri Global Limited, B.N. Agritech Limited and Salasar Balaji Overseas Private Limited with BN Agrochem is intended to consolidate related operations and improve procurement, inventory, facility utilisation, working capital and cash-flow management; the Scheme received the requisite NOC from BSE Limited in March 2026 and approval from the Competition Commission of India in April 2026, and remains subject to sanction by the National Company Law Tribunal. Second, a strategic investment in Epitome Industries India Limited through Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares provides a pathway into downstream manufacturing: Epitome is described as developing manufacturing facilities across multiple locations in India focused on oleochemicals, speciality ingredients and other value-added products. No commissioning dates, site names or project sizes are given for those Epitome facilities. Over the longer term the Company says it may evaluate origin-linked sourcing and selective upstream integration, including palm-oil plantation participation, all expressly subject to feasibility, approvals, capital allocation and execution decisions.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India remains one of the world's largest consumers and importers of edible oils; during the 2025-26 oil year domestic edible oil production was estimated at 9.6 million tonnes while imports were projected at around 16.7 million tonnes, reflecting strong domestic demand across the edible oil value chain
- The edible oil and agri-commodity industries are witnessing structural transformation driven by evolving consumer preferences, changing global trade dynamics and increasing demand for value-added products
- Regional diversity of India's edible oil market (mustard in the north and east; coconut, soybean and sunflower elsewhere), with increasing domestic and international demand for soybean oil contributing to market growth
- Value capture is intended to increase by converting common agricultural and oil-based feedstocks into multiple products, applications and market channels
- The proposed merger is intended to strengthen the operating core while the Epitome investment expands the pathway into downstream manufacturing and value-added applications, creating avenues for margin expansion and product diversification over time
- Centralised procurement and inventory management can enhance visibility and negotiating leverage; better facility utilisation can improve operating efficiency; tighter working-capital and cash-flow management can support more disciplined growth

risks.note: BRSR Section A reports one business activity, Trading of Edible Oils, at 100% of turnover, and one product line, wholesale trading of edible oils (NIC 46305), at 100% of turnover. There is no second revenue stream to absorb a downturn in edible-oil trading.

risks.risk: Commodity price volatility across the agri-oils chain
risks.note: The MD&A cautionary statement names commodity prices and market dynamics among the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. As a trader of refined soyabean oil, crude palm oil and crude soyabean oil the Company is directly exposed to price movement between purchase and sale, and the Corporate Governance Report states that commodity price and foreign exchange hedging is not applicable as the Company is not associated with hedging activities.

risks.risk: Import dependence and trade-policy exposure of the Indian edible oil market
risks.note: The MD&A notes that against estimated domestic edible oil production of 9.6 million tonnes in the 2025-26 oil year, imports were projected at around 16.7 million tonnes. Government policies, regulatory developments and changing global trade dynamics, all named in the cautionary statement, therefore transmit directly into sourcing economics.

risks.risk: Execution and approval risk on the proposed Scheme of Amalgamation
risks.note: The amalgamation of A1 Agri Global Limited, B.N. Agritech Limited and Salasar Balaji Overseas Private Limited is central to the stated strategy but remains subject to sanction by the National Company Law Tribunal despite receipt of the BSE NOC in March 2026 and CCI approval in April 2026. The Board also had to approve amendments to the Scheme in December 2025.

risks.risk: Feasibility, capital-allocation and execution risk on the diversification agenda
risks.note: The Company repeatedly qualifies its move into oleochemicals, ingredients, consumer FMCG, biofuels and palm-oil plantation as subject to feasibility, approvals, capital allocation and execution decisions, and its Important note on Strategic Statements warns these initiatives should not be read as currently operational or committed. The downstream pathway depends on Epitome Industries India Limited, an investee rather than a controlled manufacturing asset.

risks.risk: Key-person dependence and a very thin organisational base
risks.note: There were 06 permanent employees as on March 31, 2026, and the BRSR states the Company had no employees other than the Board of Directors and Key Managerial Personnel during the reporting period, and no workers. Permanent-employee turnover was 50% in FY2025-26 and 100% in FY2023-24. Board and KMP churn during the year included a CEO change, a director resignation and a CFO change.

BSE levied two Standard Operating Procedure fines during the year: INR 76,700 for delay in submitting financial results under Regulation 33 for the quarter and year ended March 31, 2025, and INR 1,22,720 for alleged non-submission of the Annual Report within the prescribed timeline, for which a waiver application is under correspondence with BSE.

risks.risk: Related-party concentration and governance oversight burden
risks.note: The 35th AGM notice seeks member approval for material related-party transactions including with B.N. Agritech Limited, potentially exceeding the INR 1000 Crore or 10% of consolidated turnover threshold, for a tenure of three years. Several counterparties are entities on which the Company own Key Managerial Personnel have significant influence or control, concentrating oversight responsibility on the Audit Committee and Board.

risks.risk: Asset-light structure with no owned manufacturing capacity
risks.note: The Corporate Governance Report states the Company does not have any plant at any location, and BRSR reports zero plants nationally and internationally against two offices. BRSR Principle 2 confirms no R&D or capex expenditure was incurred because the Company is engaged in trading activities. Value capture therefore rests on trading margins and on assets held by investee or transferor entities rather than an owned asset base.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: BN Agrochem Limited (formerly BN Holdings Limited) is an asset-light agri-oils enterprise engaged in the wholesale trading of refined soyabean oil, crude palm oil and crude soyabean oil, which accounted for 100% of turnover in FY2025-26.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company is an operating agri-oils enterprise whose business activities and interests span agricultural commodities, oilseeds, edible oils and related products. It currently participates in the trading of refined soyabean oil, crude palm oil and crude soyabean oil, primarily serving wholesale and business customers, while its broader operating scope extends across oilseeds, solvent extraction, extracted oil cakes, refined oils and allied value chains. Its stated ambition is to progressively integrate a larger part of the agri-oils value chain, from origin and sourcing through processing, refining, ingredients, oleochemicals and bio-based derivatives to consumer products and distribution.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- BN Holdings Europe Limited — subsidiary: Wholly Owned Subsidiary, 100% held directly by the listed entity; incorporated at London on February 17, 2024; does not participate in the BRSR initiatives of the listed entity
- BN Agrochem Singapore PTE Limited — subsidiary: Overseas subsidiary at Singapore, incorporated February 14, 2024; classified in BRSR item 23 as a step down subsidiary with 0.03% held directly by the listed entity; does not participate in the BRSR initiatives of the listed entity
- BNPB Industries Liberia Corporation — subsidiary: Step down subsidiary in Liberia, wholly owned subsidiary of BN Holdings Europe Limited; 0% held directly by the listed entity; incorporated/acquired 19.12.2024; does not participate in the BRSR initiatives of the listed entity
- B.N. Corporate Park Private Limited — related party: Entity on which one or more Key Managerial Personnel have significant influence or control
- Unified Professionals & Digital Services Private Limited — related party: Entity on which one or more Key Managerial Personnel have significant influence or control
- B.N. Agritech Limited — related party: Entity on which one or more Key Managerial Personnel have significant influence or control; also a transferor company under the proposed Scheme of Amalgamation and the named counterparty in the material related-party transaction resolution placed before the 35th AGM
- Epitome Industries (KA) India Limited — related party: Entity on which one or more Key Managerial Personnel have significant influence or control
- Epitome Industries (WB) India Limited — related party: Entity on which one or more Key Managerial Personnel have significant influence or control
- Epitome Industries India Limited — related party: Investee company in which BN Agrochem holds a strategic investment through Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares; described as developing manufacturing facilities across multiple locations in India focused on oleochemicals and speciality ingredients
- A1 Agri Global Limited — related party: Transferor company under the proposed Scheme of Amalgamation with BN Agrochem
- Salasar Balaji Overseas Private Limited — related party: Transferor company under the proposed Scheme of Amalgamation with BN Agrochem

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Trading - Edible Oils:** Refined soyabean oil, Crude palm oil, Crude soyabean oil, Wholesale trading of Edible Oils (NIC Code 46305)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Domestic India - wholesale and business (B2B) customers
- Wholesale customers for edible crude soya and palm oils
- Markets served: 1 Indian state; no international markets; exports not applicable

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India remains one of the world's largest consumers and importers of edible oils; during the 2025-26 oil year domestic edible oil production was estimated at 9.6 million tonnes while imports were projected at around 16.7 million tonnes, reflecting strong domestic demand across the edible oil value chain
- The edible oil and agri-commodity industries are witnessing structural transformation driven by evolving consumer preferences, changing global trade dynamics and increasing demand for value-added products
- Regional diversity of India's edible oil market (mustard in the north and east; coconut, soybean and sunflower elsewhere), with increasing domestic and international demand for soybean oil contributing to market growth
- Value capture is intended to increase by converting common agricultural and oil-based feedstocks into multiple products, applications and market channels
- The proposed merger is intended to strengthen the operating core while the Epitome investment expands the pathway into downstream manufacturing and value-added applications, creating avenues for margin expansion and product diversification over time
- Centralised procurement and inventory management can enhance visibility and negotiating leverage; better facility utilisation can improve operating efficiency; tighter working-capital and cash-flow management can support more disciplined growth

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Integrate the operating core: execute the proposed amalgamation of A1 Agri Global Limited, B.N. Agritech Limited and Salasar Balaji Overseas Private Limited, and strengthen procurement, inventory, facility, customer and working-capital linkages
- Scale value-added manufacturing: build participation in food ingredients, oleochemicals, specialty derivatives and allied downstream products, including through the strategic CCPS investment in Epitome Industries India Limited
- Deepen consumer participation: expand consumer-facing products and branded opportunities where the Company can build differentiated market positions
- Strengthen feedstock security: develop diversified sourcing and evaluate selective upstream integration, including origin-linked sourcing and palm-oil plantation opportunities, where economically attractive
- Improve capital and working-capital efficiency: align growth with disciplined capital allocation, cash-flow visibility and prudent balance-sheet management
- Build an institutional-grade platform: create governance, reporting, operating systems and scale suitable for long-term banking, institutional capital and strategic partnerships
- Progress from commodity participation to value-added manufacturing, from B2B supply to deeper customer and consumer engagement, and from individual operating businesses to a connected platform ('From Agriculture to Consumer. From Commodity to Specialty.')
- Build a longer-term business architecture spanning Agri & Sourcing, Edible Oils & Processing, Oilseed Co-products, Food Ingredients, Oleochemicals & Derivatives, Consumer FMCG, Biofuels & Green Products, and Distribution & Supply Chain, developed progressively rather than simultaneously

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Existing participation in edible oils and related agri-oil products provides commercial relationships, market intelligence and a base from which to integrate adjacent value pools
- Proposed amalgamation of A1 Agri Global Limited, B.N. Agritech Limited and Salasar Balaji Overseas Private Limited is intended to centralise procurement and inventory management, improve facility utilisation and strengthen working-capital and cash-flow management
- Strategic investment in Epitome Industries India Limited through Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares creates a pathway into oleochemicals, speciality ingredients and other value-added oil-derived products
- Ability to convert common agricultural and oil-based feedstocks into multiple products, applications and market channels, broadening monetisation opportunities
- Overseas subsidiary footprint in Singapore, London and Liberia supporting origin-linked sourcing optionality
